assessment: Many brain circuits, particularly those found in mammalian sensory cortices, need to respond rapidly to stimuli while at the same time avoiding pathological, runaway excitation. Over several years, many theoretical studies have attempted to explain how cortical circuits achieve these goals through interactions between inhibitory and excitatory cells. This study adds to this literature by showing how synaptic short-term depression can stabilise strong positive feedback in a circuit under a variety of plausible scenarios, allowing strong, rapid and stimulus-specific responses.
